title: Iterating a dictionary with freed nodes as keys can cause game window to hang indefinitely
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.dev4.official [755fa449c], v4.6.2.stable.official [71f334935] (+web editor v4.6.2)

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev4 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - AMD Ryzen 5 7600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.75 GiB memory

### Issue description

If nodes are used as dictionary keys and freed, iterating the dictionary can cause the game window to hang indefinitely.  
Doesn't happen with every freed node, but reproduces very consistently after a few repetitions.

Originally noticed this when my project would sometimes crash after changing scenes with get_tree().change_scene_to_packed but I managed to narrow it down to a script that was iterating a dictionary with nodes as keys, where the nodes would become freed on scene change.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add nodes as dictionary keys
2. Free the nodes
3. Iterate the dictionary

```gdscript
extends Node3D

@export var do_crash: bool = true

var dict: Dictionary

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	# add nodes as dict keys and free them
	if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
		print("add")
		var node := Node.new()
		dict[node] = true
		node.queue_free()
	
	# iterate dictionary to crash
	if do_crash:
		for n in dict:
			pass
	pass
```

Press space to add freed nodes into the dictionary.  
If do_crash is enabled, the dictionary is iterated every frame and will cause a hang after a few nodes are added.
